Subject: Re: Pilot questions — chat capture and DPA redlines

Hi Rishi —

Thanks for the demo last week. Our legal and privacy teams reviewed the draft DPA and we flagged a couple of operational asks before we can sign:

- We need an explicit prohibition on using live chat transcripts for model improvement (no-training/no-adaptive clause) for US consumer accounts subject to CCPA.
- For records that contain CCPA-covered personal information we require onshore key management (US KMS) + evidence of key custody in US.
- We need an export pathway for transcripts (monthly) to our secure SFTP endpoint; please confirm retention / redaction options prior to export.
- Please provide your current subprocessor list and a short proof of controls for any vendor that could see plaintext transcripts.

Attached: ProctorCare_DPA_redline_v1.pdf — redlines in track changes.

Can your team confirm these operational paths and an estimated timeline for evidence delivery (SOC2 extracts / attestation)?

Thanks,
Susan Liu
Senior Counsel — Privacy
ProctorCare

Susan —

Appreciate the clear list. Summary/next steps from our side:

1) No-training: We can enable a tenant-level "no-model-improvement" toggle that prevents any training/weight updates or retention of prompts/responses in any training pipelines. We'll provide an ops runbook and an attestation template.

2) KMS / onshore: We support customer-controlled KMS; for ProctorCare we can provision an onshore AWS KMS key in us-east-1 and provide key policy documentation. We will include audit logs showing key usage (exportable).

3) Export pathway: We can implement a scheduled export (SFTP push) and/or one-off SFTP transfer; exports can be filtered/redacted to remove PII fields prior to transfer if required. Need to confirm whether you prefer S3-to-SFTP or direct push.

4) Subprocessors: I'll attach our evidence checklist (linked) and pull the current subprocessor inventory for any vendors with potential plaintext access.

Attachments: redwood-evidence-checklist.pdf — initial mapping of required artifacts (SOC2 sections, KMS audit extracts, subprocessors).

Can Kimberly and David weigh in on runbook timeline? Susan — if you can indicate (a) whether SFTP must be from static IPs and (b) preferred cadence (monthly/weekly), we will scope work and turn around an operational plan by EOD Monday.

Best,
Rishi

Subject: Re: Pilot questions — chat capture and DPA redlines

Susan / Rishi / team —

Thanks for the questions, Susan. Operational proposal below (we'll convert to a short-runbook and attach to the DPA amendment):

1) No-training implementation
- Tenant-level "no-model-improvement" flag enabled for ProctorCare. When enabled, we drop prompts/responses from all model-improvement buckets and disable any adaptive inference logging.
- Evidence: monthly signed attestation + exportable system audit showing flag state and absence of training jobs referencing the tenant ID.

2) KMS / onshore
- We will provision a customer-managed AWS KMS key in us-east-1. KMS access logs (CloudTrail) will be included in the evidence package; we'll provide a snapshot proving keys never left the region.

3) Export pathway & retention
- Scheduled monthly SFTP push to sftp.proctorcare-secure.com from a static IP range (we will provide IPs and host key); files will be gzipped and optionally PII-redacted per template.
- Retention: default 30 days for live chat transcripts (configurable down to 7d) prior to export; retention can be shortened on request and we will include purge confirmations in evidence.

4) Subprocessors & controls
- We will deliver a current subprocessor inventory and mark any subprocessors with potential plaintext access. For those, we will provide the minimal control artifacts (NDA, SOC2 section summary, encryption-at-rest details).

5) Attestation cadence & signing
- Proposed cadence: monthly attestation (DocuSign) + quarterly evidence bundle (SOC2 extracts, KMS audit snapshot, export logs).

Next steps:
- Rishi / David: draft the short ops-runbook and the attestation template (we'll attach to the DPA amendment).
- Rishi: confirm the static IP range and timeline for KMS provisioning (we estimate 5 business days after DPA amendment).
- Susan: confirm that monthly cadence + SFTP push meets legal's minimum.

Attaching ops-runbook draft: ops-runbook-draft.docx (internal). I'll also upload a redacted subprocessor list to the shared drive and send the link separately.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30m call Monday to align.

Kimberly Park
Head of Customer Security Operations — Redwood Inference
